body:
Oh wow, it's indeed applying `TSR` instead of `TRS` transformation.
I think I've never noticed this before as I always use `draw_set_transform_matrix` instead. Which you can of course use as a workaround:

```gdscript
extends Button
var tex := preload("res://line.png")

func _draw():
	if tex:
		var angle_radians: float = deg_to_rad(1.0)
		
		var t := Vector2(400, 400)
		var r := angle_radians
		var s := Vector2(100, 1)
		
		var T := Transform2D().translated(t)
		var R := Transform2D().rotated(r)
		var S := Transform2D().scaled(s)
		
		# These are equivalent (the unexpected behavior):
		draw_set_transform(t, r, s)
		#draw_set_transform_matrix(Transform2D().rotated(r).scaled(s).translated(t))
		#draw_set_transform_matrix(T * S * R)

		# These are equivalent (the expected behavior):
		#draw_set_transform_matrix(Transform2D().scaled(s).rotated(r).translated(t))
		#draw_set_transform_matrix(T * R * S)
		
		draw_texture(tex, Vector2.ZERO)
```

Changing the current `draw_set_transform` behavior will break things for someone who is relying on it (only in cases when passing both non-zero rotation and non-unit scale at the same time though). Nevertheless I do consider this as a bug.

---

Here's an example ([angledTest_v2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22850579/angledTest_v2.zip)) showing the current behavior is not consistent with the rest of the engine: a Node2D (the drawer, with the script below attached) with a child Sprite2D (with `show_behind_parent = true`).
```gdscript
@tool
extends Node2D

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	queue_redraw()

func _draw() -> void:
	var sprite: Sprite2D = $Sprite2D
	
	draw_set_transform(sprite.position, sprite.rotation, sprite.scale)
	#draw_set_transform_matrix(sprite.transform)
	
	var rect := sprite.get_rect()
	draw_rect(rect, Color.VIOLET, false)
	draw_line(Vector2(rect.position.x, 0), Vector2(rect.end.x, 0), Color.GREEN)
	draw_line(Vector2(0, rect.position.y), Vector2(0, rect.end.y), Color.RED)
```

- For `draw_set_transform(sprite.position, sprite.rotation, sprite.scale)` the drawing mismatches the child sprite in case of non-uniform scale (aka when the order of applying the rotation/scale does matter).
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60c2fe7b-068d-4b9d-8e3b-3351b538b25c)
Note that the drawing would of course also mismatch in case of non-zero `sprite.skew` as `draw_set_transform` does not support skewing (it should be trivial to add it as an additional parameter defaulting to `0.0` though). But that's beside the point here.

- For `draw_set_transform_matrix(sprite.transform)` the drawing matches the child sprite regardless of rotation/scale (and skew).
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0db7c092-2d45-485b-a91b-8e8eed2f9692)
